```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)

pacman::p_load("lubridate", "glue", "RcppRoll", "broom", "fmxdat")
# Load tidyverse last so that dplyr's first() and last() are used
library(tidyverse)

# Question 3 functions (code/ folder of this question)
list.files('code/', full.names = T, recursive = T) %>% .[grepl('.R', .)] %>% as.list() %>% walk(~source(.))

# Shared functions from the root project

```

```{r Q3_Data}
Active_Manager_Peers <- read_rds("data/Active_Managers.rds")
ABC_Fund <- read_rds("data/ABC_Fund.rds")
Idx_Daily <- read_rds("data/Index_Returns_Daily.rds")
Cons <- read_rds("data/Index_Constituents.rds")
```

```{r Q3_Monthly}
# Monthly returns for the Capped SWIX and the style indexes
# This functions chains daily returns into an index, keep the last trading day of each month and take month-on-month returns
Idx_Monthly <-
  Idx_Daily %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  group_by(Tickers) %>%
  mutate(Index = cumprod(1 + Returns)) %>%
  mutate(YM = format(date, "%Y%B")) %>%
  group_by(Tickers, YM) %>%
  filter(date == last(date)) %>%
  group_by(Tickers) %>%
  mutate(Ret = Index / lag(Index) - 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(Ret)) %>%
  select(YM, Tickers, Ret)
```

```{r Q3_BM}
# Benchmark (Capped SWIX) monthly returns
BM_Monthly <- Idx_Monthly %>% filter(Tickers == "J433") %>% select(YM, BM_Monthly = Ret)
```

```{r Q3_Funds}
# Peers and ABC Fund in one data frame, with the same month label for joining
Funds <- bind_rows(Active_Manager_Peers, ABC_Fund) %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(YM = format(date, "%Y%B"))
```

## Overview

- This presentation will look at how ABC Fund compares to its active manager peers, purely from a returns perspective. (The Capped SWIX is used as the market benchmark throughout).
- It will look at:
    - How much of the returns of active managers simply follow the market
    - What drives the returns of ABC Fund compared to its peers
    - How ABC Fund has performed relative to its peers over time
    - How ABC Fund performs when the returns of individual stocks differ a lot (market dispersion)

```{r Q3_Roll_Beta, cache = TRUE}
# Rolling 36 month regression of each fund on the Capped SWIX (months with benchmark data only)
Manager_list <- Funds %>% filter(YM %in% BM_Monthly$YM) %>% group_split(Name)

Rolling_Beta <- Manager_list %>%
  map_df(~Q3_Roll_Regression(., BM_Monthly, Nsel = 36, Silent = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(date)
```

## ABC Fund is less dependent on the market than its peers

```{r Q3_Beta_Plot}
Q3_Beta_Boxplot(Rolling_Beta, Months_back = 60, Fund = "ABC_Fund")
```

## Explanation

- Most active managers have a high market sensitivity, which means that their returns are mostly similar to that of the market.
- ABC Fund has a lower market sensitivity than most of its peers. Therefore, a larger part of its returns comes from its own investment decisions.

```{r Q3_Factor_Data}
# Market and style index returns in columns
Factors <- Idx_Monthly %>%
  filter(Tickers %in% c("J433", "STXVALJ433", "STXMOMJ433", "STXLVLJ433", "J202")) %>%
  spread(Tickers, Ret) %>%
  select(YM, Market = J433, Value = STXVALJ433, Momentum = STXMOMJ433, Low_Vol = STXLVLJ433, Small_Caps = J202)

# ABC Fund returns joined to the factor returns
ABC_df <- Funds %>%
  #Chooses one fund (ABC)
  filter(Name == "ABC_Fund") %>%
  select(YM, Returns) %>%
    # Month end dates differ (join by YM)
  left_join(Factors, by = "YM") %>%
  drop_na()

# Average peer return each month joined to the factor returns
Peer_df <- Funds %>%
  filter(Name != "ABC_Fund") %>%
  group_by(YM) %>%
    # Average return across all peers in each month
  summarise(Returns = mean(Returns, na.rm = T)) %>%
  left_join(Factors, by = "YM") %>%
  drop_na()
```

```{r Q3_Factor_Reg}
# Returns regressed on the market and style returns
# lm used directly as tidyfit::regress returned an error (slice_id not found)
lm_ABC  <- lm(Returns ~ Market + Value + Momentum + Low_Vol + Small_Caps, data = ABC_df)
lm_Peer <- lm(Returns ~ Market + Value + Momentum + Low_Vol + Small_Caps, data = Peer_df)

# Exposures of both in one table (intercept removed)
Loadings <-
  bind_rows(lm_ABC %>% broom::tidy() %>% mutate(Name = "ABC Fund"),
    lm_Peer %>% broom::tidy() %>% mutate(Name = "Average peer")) %>%
    # Intercept removed so that only the factor exposures are shown
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")
```

## What drives ABC Fund's returns?

```{r Q3_Factor_Plot}
g_fac <- Loadings %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(term, estimate, fill = Name), stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  labs(title = "What drives the returns of ABC Fund compared to the average peer",
       subtitle = "Above zero: returns move with that part of the market. Below zero: returns move against it",
       x = "", y = "Exposure") +
  fmxdat::theme_fmx() + fmxdat::fmx_fills()

g_fac
```

## Explanation

- The average peer's returns move mostly with the overall market.
- ABC Fund's returns depend less on the overall market and lean more towards value stocks.
- Therefore, ABC Fund offers clients a different source of returns to most of the industry.

```{r Q3_Share_Data}
# Rolling 3 year annualised return of every fund
Roll_Funds <- Funds %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  group_by(Name) %>%
  mutate(RollRet = RcppRoll::roll_prod(1+Returns, n = 36, fill = NA, align = "right")^(12/36) - 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(RollRet))

# ABC Fund's rolling return in its own column
ABC_Roll <- Roll_Funds %>% filter(Name == "ABC_Fund") %>% select(YM, ABC = RollRet)

# Share of peers with a lower rolling return than ABC Fund each month
df_comp <- Roll_Funds %>%
  filter(Name != "ABC_Fund") %>%
  left_join(ABC_Roll, by = "YM") %>%
  filter(!is.na(ABC)) %>%
  mutate(XS = ABC - RollRet) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(Proportion = sum(XS>0)/n())
```

## ABC Fund against its peers over time

```{r Q3_Share_Plot}
g_share <- df_comp %>%
  ggplot() +
  # Green when ABC Fund beat more than half of its peers, red when it beat fewer
  geom_ribbon(aes(date, ymin = 0.5, ymax = ifelse(Proportion > 0.5, Proportion, 0.5)), fill = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(date, ymin = ifelse(Proportion < 0.5, Proportion, 0.5), ymax = 0.5), fill = "darkred", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(date, Proportion), colour = "grey30", size = 1) +
  # Half of peers beaten
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "ABC Fund has outperformed most of its peers for most of the last decade",
       subtitle = "Share of peers with a lower rolling 3 year return than ABC Fund",
       caption = "Green: ABC Fund beat more than half of its peers. Red: ABC Fund beat fewer than half.",
       x = "", y = "Share of peers beaten") +
  fmxdat::theme_fmx()

finplot(g_share, x.date.dist = "1 year", x.date.type = "%Y", x.vert = T, y.pct = T, y.pct_acc = 1)
```

## Explanation

- ABC Fund had a higher rolling 3 year return than most of its peers in almost every period since 2015.
- Its performance has been weaker recently, which can be expected for a fund that is quite different from its peers.

```{r Q3_Disp, cache = TRUE}
# Capped SWIX constituents and benchmark returns
J433_Cons <- Cons %>% filter(Index == "Capped SWIX")
BM <- Idx_Daily %>% filter(Tickers == "J433") %>% select(date, BM = Returns)

# Rolling 12 month (250 day) dispersion
ann_disp <- Dispersion_Prep(df_used = J433_Cons, BMUse = BM, BMSel = "weight", NSel = 250)
```

```{r Q3_Enviro}
# Month-end dispersion
Disp_M <-
  ann_disp %>%
  mutate(YM = format(date, "%Y%B")) %>%
  group_by(YM) %>% filter(date == last(date)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(YM, Disp = Dispersion_W)

# Fund returns joined to dispersion, split into high, low and other, then averaged
Enviro_Tab <-
  Q3_Rel_12m(Funds, BM_Monthly, Fund = "ABC_Fund") %>%
  left_join(Disp_M, by = "YM") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(Disp)) %>%
  mutate( hidisp = quantile(Disp, 0.85),
          lodisp = quantile(Disp, 0.25)) %>%
  mutate(Enviro = ifelse(Disp > hidisp, "High dispersion",
                         ifelse(Disp < lodisp, "Low dispersion",
                                "Other"))) %>%
  group_by(Enviro, Group) %>%
  summarise(XS = mean(XS))
```

## ABC Fund has not outperformed its peers when dispersion is high

```{r Q3_Dispersion}
g_disp <-
  Enviro_Tab %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(Enviro, XS, fill = Group), stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  labs(title = "ABC Fund compared to the average peer when market dispersion is high and low",
       subtitle = "Average 12 month return above the market (Capped SWIX)",
              caption = "High dispersion: the top 15% of months, when stock returns differed most from the market.",
       x = "", y = "Return above the market") +
  fmxdat::theme_fmx() + fmxdat::fmx_fills()

fmxdat::finplot(g_disp, y.pct = T, y.pct_acc = 0.1)
```

## Explanation
- Market dispersion measures how much the returns of individual stocks differ from the return of the market. When it is high, active managers have more opportunity to differ from the market.
- ABC Fund did better than the average peer in normal and calmer markets, which make up most of the period.
- In periods of very high dispersion, ABC Fund performed in line with its peers.

## Summary

- ABC Fund is less dependent on the market than most active managers, whose returns largely follow the market.
- Its returns lean towards value stocks, so it offers clients a different source of returns to most of its peers.
- It has outperformed most of its peers for most of the last decade.
- Therefore, ABC Fund adds something different to a portfolio of typical active funds, which makes a strong case for including it in client portfolios.
